newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-NYMEX supported, has momentum to rise.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-NYMEX supported, has momentum to rise.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20

* The uptrend is seen continuing with the belt of resistance between $19.50-$20.00 broken down on Tuesday now providing good support against what analysts see as a brief downside. * "The ultimate long term target remains the $22.40 of May 16, but first WTI must stay convincingly above $20.

Disappointing API stock data set NYMEX crude and products futures lower in overnight ACCESS trade but technical analysts see good supports in place and enough upside momentum to keep the markets heading higher.

WTI is seen continuing to extend the recent uptrend once the API-related selling pressure peters out. The market pushed higher on Tuesday bursting resistance on a short-term downtrend line at $19.89 to close 12 cents a barrel over the psychological $20 barrier.
This trend is seen continuing with the belt of resistance represented between $19.50 and $20.00 broken down on Tuesday now providing good support against what analysts see as a brief downside.
"The ultimate long term target remains the $22.40 of May 16, but first we must stay convincingly above $20," one analyst said.

Victor Yu, analyst at Refco, said he was surprised that the market had read so much downside into the APIs. "It's now a question of whether the market can stay down below $20, but if it doesn't make it back today there are some good supports at previous resistance levels in the $19.65-70 region", Yu said.
He said RSIs continued to offer room to move higher but saw Fibonacci resistance coming in at $20.47 and $20.90 providing a cap.
Unleaded gasoline filled the gap-down opened in mid-June, the top of which was at 59.15 cents when it traded up to 59.25, on Tuesday.

Analysts said this level may be achievable again soon but the market would need to hold support around 58 cents today if the longer term target of 67.60 cents from May 23 and the current uptrend of the last week is to remain intact.
Heating oil continues to ride the fourth wave of uptrend since the fall that took it from 75.70 cents a gallon down to 52.15 cents.

Two of the previous three peaks have achieved 59 cents before rallies petered out and despite some small correction today analysts said momentum and strength indicators remain in neutral territory leaving sufficient room for further improvements.
